$PDYN Palladyne AI — preliminary Q2 2026 revenue of $5.8 million

•	Revenue rose approximately 480% year-over-year and 66% sequentially.

•	Backlog grew to approximately $24.0 million, up from $17.3 million in Q1.

•	Roughly $12.5 million in new customer programs and contract awards were added during the quarter.

•	Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities held steady at approximately $44.0 million as of June 30, 2026.

$RKLB Rocket Lab — Morgan Stanley reiterates Overweight, raises bull case to $293

•	Morgan Stanley maintains its Overweight rating with a base-case price target of $105.

•	The firm raised its bull-case price target to $293, up from $185.

•	The upgraded bull case reflects the Iridium acquisition, upside from launch and connectivity businesses, and Rocket Lab’s shift toward a more vertically integrated space platform.

Blue Origin is raising $10 billion in its first outside funding round, with Jeff Bezos personally contributing an additional $2 billion.

•	The round values Blue Origin at $130 billion, excluding the new funds.

•	Coatue Management is expected to lead with a $4 billion commitment; Bezos’ family office is a major investor in Coatue’s Innovative Strategies Fund.

•	Bezos himself is contributing $2 billion, with the remaining $4 billion expected from large institutional investors.

•	This is Blue Origin’s first time raising outside capital, marking a shift from relying solely on Bezos as its backer.

•	Bezos has said he believes Blue Origin could one day be worth more than Amazon, and the raise may reduce his need to fund the company by selling Amazon shares.

$RUN Sunrun launches a distributed AI compute pilot using its home energy network.

•	The pilot uses residential solar and battery systems to host distributed AI compute nodes.

•	It follows a proof-of-concept that showed revenue generation and strong demand.

•	Sunrun plans to deploy compute nodes across its 1.1 million-customer network.

•	The company will sell AI inference capacity to enterprise compute buyers.

•	Participating homeowners will be compensated for hosting compute nodes.

•	Sunrun cites AI inference demand growing about 35% annually, with McKinsey projecting inference workloads will exceed training workloads by 2030.

•	The company says its distributed model enables faster compute deployment than traditional data centers.

$LAES and $GFS team up to build secure chips for the post-quantum era.

•	SEALSQ and GlobalFoundries signed a strategic MoU to co-develop secure semiconductor technologies.

•	The partnership targets post-quantum cryptography (PQC), secure chiplets, and quantum computing.

•	The companies will co-develop pre-certified PQC security IP and chiplet hardware security modules.

•	Collaboration also covers CryoCMOS ASIC development for future quantum computing systems.

•	The initiative pairs GlobalFoundries’ U.S. manufacturing capabilities with SEALSQ’s secure semiconductor expertise.

•	It aims to support sovereign and trusted semiconductor supply chains in the U.S. and Europe.

•	The work builds on GlobalFoundries’ Quantum Technology Solutions business and SEALSQ’s quantum investments.

$HOOD — Compass Point sees a Q2 EBITDA beat coming, lifts PT to $130

•	Analyst Ed Engel raised the price target to $130.00 from $107.00, up 21.5%, while maintaining Buy — implying about 15.15% upside from the current $112.90 price.

•	Compass Point forecasts an 18% Q2 EBITDA beat driven by higher volumes and take rates.

•	The firm sees further upside to 2H26 estimates from higher take rates, prediction volumes, and a 10% workforce reduction announced on June 16.

•	Q2 prediction volumes ran 57% above 4Q25 despite a softer sports calendar, and Engel expects prediction markets to accelerate further in 2H during football season.

•	Risks flagged include crypto remaining in a bear market; shares previously sold off about 50% after Robinhood missed two consecutive quarters.

$GRAB — BofA Securities maintains Buy rating on Grab Holdings, price target set at $5.20

•	BofA has cited strong fundamentals in Grab’s core mobility and delivery businesses, along with low competition and improving margins, in its earlier bullish calls on the stock.

$NET Cloudflare and OpenAI launch a pilot to improve AI search.

•	The pilot tests whether Cloudflare’s network signals can improve AI search indexing and crawling.

•	It uses real-time signals like content freshness, traffic quality, and page changes to make AI answers more accurate and timely.

•	Cloudflare brings network insights from infrastructure serving more than 20% of the web, while OpenAI provides search capabilities and real user queries for testing.

$HON — Honeywell Aerospace signs an MOU with Enigma Aerospace on Phoenix autonomous aircraft systems

•	The two companies will explore integrating Honeywell’s navigation, mission systems, and electronic warfare capabilities onto Enigma’s Phoenix Series UAS.

•	Focus areas include resilient PNT, alternative navigation, defensive electronic warfare, secure communications, defensive cyber, and compact mission systems.

•	As an initial step, they plan to evaluate Honeywell’s VersaWave SATCOM, Ground Control Station, and ONEBOX flight controller on the Phoenix aircraft.

•	Honeywell says the goal is to help Phoenix operate in GPS-denied and communications-degraded environments and reach warfighters faster.

$GWH — ESS Tech launches Bridge, a modular sodium-ion storage system

•	ESS introduced Bridge, a modular sodium-ion battery energy storage system for grid-scale, AI data centers, critical infrastructure, and commercial use.

•	The base system is 1.2 MWh and can be stacked to 4.8 MWh.

•	It supports charge and discharge durations from 1 to 16+ hours.

•	ESS says the launch follows more than $1 billion in early-stage customer opportunities since entering sodium-ion batteries.

Alibaba (BABA) jumped about 10% in premarket trading after signs of stronger AI growth and better profitability.

•	Investors liked news that instant-commerce losses narrowed in June and overall profitability held steady.

•	Sentiment also improved on reports that Alibaba Cloud’s AI growth accelerated and its AI services were consolidated under the Qwen brand.

•	A Frost & Sullivan report said Alibaba Cloud held 40.1% of China’s full-stack AI cloud market, ahead of Baidu, ByteDance’s Volcano Engine, and SenseTime combined.

•	The same report said China is now consuming about 140 trillion tokens per day, up more than 1,000x in two years.

•	Separately, a U.S. federal judge temporarily paused the Pentagon’s ban on Alibaba hiring U.S. lobbying firms while the legal challenge continues.

Google is banning Chrome extensions that support prediction markets, starting August 1, 2026.

•	The updated Chrome Web Store policy classifies prediction markets as prohibited products.

•	Extensions that enable real-money trading on prediction outcomes will no longer be allowed.

•	Google also tightened privacy rules so extension data collection must be strictly tied to the extension’s disclosed purpose.

•	The policy update takes effect on August 1, 2026.

$AVAV shares climb 7% after AeroVironment lays out its fiscal 2030 growth roadmap.

•	Shares rose about 7% following the company’s investor day presentation.

•	AeroVironment targets 15%-20% organic revenue growth through fiscal 2030, aiming to roughly double revenue by then.

•	Fiscal 2030 adjusted EBITDA margin is targeted at 18%-20%, up from 14.5% projected for fiscal 2026.

•	R&D spending is set to rise to 7%-9% of revenue by fiscal 2030, up from 6% projected in fiscal 2026, supporting future defense technology development.

•	Fiscal 2027 revenue guidance is set at $2.125-$2.225 billion, implying about 10% year-over-year growth at the midpoint.

•	Fiscal 2027 adjusted EBITDA is expected at $305-$325 million, with a 14.5% margin.

$GEHC GE HealthCare expands its Mayo Clinic cancer research partnership.

•	GE HealthCare and Mayo Clinic announced the MI-BET collaboration to study a more personalized approach to radioligand therapy for advanced prostate cancer.

•	The study will use GE HealthCare’s StarGuide SPECT/CT and MIM Software’s MIM LesionID Pro to track tumor response during treatment.

•	The work builds on the 2023 Strategic Radiology Research Alliance between Mayo Clinic and GE HealthCare.

IBM and Red Hat launch Lightwell to harden open source for the AI era.

•	Lightwell Network and Lightwell Clearinghouse Premier are now commercially available.

•	Lightwell Network includes more than 6,500 remediated, digitally signed, and certified application-layer dependencies across ecosystems like Java and Python.

•	IBM and Red Hat say the platform uses an AI-powered remediation engine to automate vulnerability fixes at scale.

Supermicro launches Kubernetes Edge AI appliances with Red Hat and Everpure.

•	The turnkey stack combines Supermicro edge servers, Red Hat OpenShift, and Portworx by Everpure.

•	It is designed to deploy and manage AI workloads across distributed edge environments.

•	The appliances come preloaded with hardware and software and are sold directly through Supermicro.
